title: Hacktron AI researchers used Claude to hack OpenAI systems in security exercise
content_md: A cybersecurity research team received a $6,500 bounty for successfully hacking OpenAI using Claude in under 72 hours during an organized exercise. Researchers from Hacktron AI gained access to OpenAI's private source code using Anthropic's Claude model. The three researchers exploited two vulnerabilities: an image processing flaw in OpenAI's Discourse-hosted community forum (via HEIC/HEIF files processed by ImageMagick and libheif) that enabled server-side code execution, and a misconfigured SSO authentication system that allowed them to take over ChatGPT and Codex employee accounts connected to OpenAI's GitHub organization. After the forum was compromised, they used Codex to create a pull request in OpenAI's internal repository to demonstrate impact. Claude Opus 5 accelerated the exploitation, producing a working exploit in approximately three hours. OpenAI patched the vulnerability 14 hours after reporting and awarded the $6,500 bounty.
